response.consequence: A payload with a `*_ids` entry that isn't side-loaded produces an array containing undefined, and the original ids are discarded. Consumers iterating the array then fail on the undefined items, or silently lose data. A null `*_ids` value throws during hydration.
response.explanation: Hydration only runs when root.__rest_serializer === "1", so it doesn't touch every object. But the new plural branch differs from the singular branch. It maps each id through _lookupSubType, which returns undefined when the id is missing from the side-loaded collection, or when Category.findById finds nothing. Those undefined values stay in the resulting array. `hydrated || []` never applies, because an array is always truthy. The code then deletes the original `*_ids` field regardless, so the unresolved ids are lost. The singular branch only deletes the id when the lookup succeeds. If obj[k] is null or not an array, `.map` throws.
response.title: Plural *_ids hydration keeps undefined entries and drops the ids unconditionally
